questions: Does the 12 mm footprint lower max_error or steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom compared with 16 mm (iteration 4)?
Do line-loss events rise at the outer sensors (+/-0.06 m) with the smaller footprint, and on which track and bend?
Does progress on the s-bend hold at or above 0.185, or does the sharper reading add lag or jitter?
Is control_effort higher or lower than iteration 4 on the s-bend, which would show whether the controller works harder with the finer signal?

intent: Test whether a smaller 12 mm sensor footprint, with the best-measured layout otherwise unchanged, gives sharper line-position readings and lower max_error on bends. The baseline is iteration 4 (58.54, the best so far), so the race isolates the footprint change. Expected: score near 58 or higher, with progress held at or above 0.185 on the s-bend and line loss at or below iteration 4 levels.
learning: Iteration 8 showed that a shorter sensor lead (y=0.03) hurts badly (41.1 vs 58.5), so y=0.05 m is the best measured lead. Radius 0.03 m and mass 0.8 kg are near their measured optima, and wheel_track is at its minimum. Footprint size is the remaining untested geometry lever. If 12 mm helps, the next step is a fine-tune of the sensor span. If it causes edge line loss, revert to 16 mm and consider a 0.07 m span.
rationale: Evidence. Iteration 8 moved the sensors forward-to-back from y=0.05 to y=0.03 m and scored 41.1, down from 58.5 at iteration 4. The s-bend progress collapsed from 0.185 to 0.056, and the oval result was unchanged. A shorter lead therefore hurts. Iteration 2 (y=0.07, confounded with a shorter, lighter body) also hurt, so y=0.05 m is the best measured sensor lead, and I keep it. Every run across all iterations still ends off_track with max_error at the 0.06 m floor. That floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which does not move for any allowed body width, so body width stays at 0.12 m. Line loss is now rare (oval 0, s-bend about 0.95, slalom about 0.85 at iteration 4), so sensor span is not the limit. Radius 0.025 gave 57.9 and 0.04 gave 41.4, so 0.03 m is near optimal. Mass 1.0 kg hurt (42.7), so 0.8 kg stays. Wheel_track is already at its 0.08 m minimum. The one geometry lever not yet tested alone is sensor footprint size. Iteration 4 used 16 mm footprints. A 12 mm footprint gives a sharper, less-averaged position reading across the tape, which may reduce the lag that drives max_error on bends. Change: sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m, with everything else held at iteration 4 values (7 sensors at y=0.05, x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.02 steps, wheel_track 0.08, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.18 x 0.12, mass 0.8). Expected result: max_error and steering_oscillation at or slightly below iteration 4, progress at or above 0.185 on the s-bend, and score near 58. Risk: the outer sensors at +/-0.06 with 12 mm footprints reach only about +/-0.066 m, so edge line loss could rise. If it does, the next step is to restore 16 mm or widen to a span of 0.07 m.
